title: Scalable Algorithms for Information Centrality Optimization via Global Edge Addition

problem.claim: The work studies global information centrality optimization by adding edges between any pair of currently non-adjacent nodes.

gap.claim: Existing edge-addition studies are restricted to edges incident to the target node, limiting use of global network structure and often producing suboptimal solutions under the same edge budget.

contributions.claim: Two scalable greedy algorithms based on gradient-guided edge selection are proposed for global information centrality optimization.
The methods use geometric interpretations, dimensionality reduction, and nearly-linear-time Laplacian solvers to approximate marginal gains and prune candidate edges.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world networks report optimization performance comparable to exact greedy strategies while substantially reducing computational time.

narrative_sequence.summary: Information centrality is presented as a useful metric for quantifying node importance in real-world applications.
Prior edge-addition optimization is limited to candidate edges incident to the target node, which can underuse global network structure and yield suboptimal solutions.

The work formulates global optimization with candidate edges between any currently non-adjacent nodes, creating a larger search space and removing the supermodularity relied on by traditional greedy approaches.
Two scalable gradient-guided greedy algorithms use geometric interpretations, dimensionality reduction, and nearly-linear-time Laplacian solvers to approximate gains and prune candidates.
Experiments on real-world networks report comparable optimization performance to exact greedy strategies with substantially lower computational time.

source_observation.claim: Global candidate-edge selection enlarges the search space and breaks the supermodularity property supporting traditional greedy approaches.

interpretation.claim: Optimization methods for globally unconstrained edge addition may need scalable approximations rather than direct application of traditional greedy methods.

application.claim: For related network optimization problems, gradient-guided candidate pruning combined with efficient linear-algebra solvers may improve scalability.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that these techniques generalize beyond the studied global information centrality optimization problem.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, edge budgets, baseline details, quantitative performance results, or computational-time reductions.
The abstract does not provide algorithmic guarantees, approximation bounds, or implementation details.
